sources.citation: Anderson (1897) An Introductory Grammar of the Sena Language, archive.org djvu full text, ACCENT section pp. 8-9
sources.quote: The accent in Sena invariably falls on the last syllable but one in a word. In case of a prefix or suffix being added to a word, the addition is treated as part of the word, and the accent shifted accordingly.

sources.citation: Anderson, W. G. 1897. An Introductory Grammar of the Sena Language spoken on the Lower Zambesi. London: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge. (archive.org item an-introductory-grammar-of-the-sena-language)
sources.quote: 'The accent in Sena invariably falls on the last syllable but one in a word. In case of a prefix or suffix being added to a word, the addition is treated as part of the word, and the accent shifted accordingly.' óna 'see', onáni 'see ye'. p. 24: with enclitic -nji 'the accent of the verb is then on its last syllable' (mu-na-funá-nji).
sources.locator: ACCENT, pp. 8-9 (PDF pp. 13-14); enclitic -nji p. 24 (PDF p. 29)

sources.citation: Torrend, Julius. 1900. Grammatica do Chisena: A grammar of the language of the Lower Zambezi. Chipanga, Zambezia: Missão do Chipanga. 293 pp. (archive.org item grammaticadochis00torruoft)
sources.quote: p. 13: 'The tonic accent in Sena, when not marked in writing, is always laid on the penultimate.' (acute written only 'where there is room for doubt'; ua, ue, ia, ie etc. count as one syllable when u/i unaccented). p. 17: 'Formal words always have the tonic accent on the penultimate; informal words [ideophones] may lay the accent on any syllable.'
sources.locator: sec. 13, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 19); ideophones ('informal words'), printed p. 17 (PDF p. 23)
